column1: # Spellings a human has confirmed, where the club's own pages published two.
# Five tab-separated columns, `#` starts a comment:
#   published
# `published` is the spelling on a club page. `confirmed` is the spelling that
# reaches past-executives.csv. `source_url` is the snapshot the published
# spelling was read from — kept because it is the evidence that the club really
# did publish it, and the evidence for whatever year that snapshot dates.
# `confirmed_by` is the role that confirmed it and `confirmed_on` the day: a
# spelling settled by a person is not derived from anything, and attributing it
# to the club page would credit the page that was wrong.
# WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A HAND EDIT. build.ts reads it and renames every
# sighting before removals and before the merge, so the correction survives the
# next rebuild. Editing the two rows into one in the CSV would not: the club's
# pages still spell it both ways, so the next rebuild splits the person again —
# the same failure removed.txt exists to prevent.
# It is also on the removal path, in both directions. A person holding two rows
# can ask to be removed under either spelling; because the correction makes them
# one name, `removed.txt` matches whichever one they wrote.
# AND A REMOVAL DELETES THEIR ROW HERE TOO. This file names a real person, so
# leaving their row behind leaves them named in this directory after they asked
# not to be. Put EVERY spelling in their row on `removed.txt` FIRST, then delete
# the row: once it is gone nothing renames the published spelling, and a list
# carrying only the confirmed one — removals match exactly — lets the next
# rebuild restore them under the spelling nobody registered. See "If someone asks
# to be removed" in README.md, which is the authoritative procedure.
# ADDING A ROW IS A HUMAN CONFIRMATION, NOT A GUESS. One character apart is
# evidence, not proof. Only add a row when somebody who knows the person has
# said which spelling is right. If nobody has, leave both rows: the roster
# reporting a discrepancy it will not resolve is the correct outcome, and a
# missing file simply means nothing has been confirmed.
# Record no contact detail here, and name a role rather than a person in
# `confirmed_by`. See README.md in this directory.
# published
Tim MacDougal
